quote: Finding your thing is the only true shortcut to life.
full_excerpt: Finding your thing is the only true shortcut to life. It's realizing that you actually have a dirt bike, so this little dirt path is perfect for you (but won't be perfect for others in cars). Everyone has a thing, you just have to find it.

quote: What does it seem like everyone else is mysteriously bad at? That's your thing.
full_excerpt: Instead of asking 'what am I great at?' – just start to pay attention to 'what does everyone else mysteriously suck at?' For me, I always wondered why other people are so bad at explanations. In school, I hated the way my teachers explained things. Too complicated, too boring.

quote: It took me 10 years to find my thing. I was a B+ founder. But in the real world, B+ doesn't get you jack sh*t.
full_excerpt: For 10 years, I tried to make being a founder my thing. I was a B+ at it. But in the real world, B+ doesn't get you jack sh*t. Then I started podcasting for fun. I started writing. I started doing the thing I thought others were mysteriously bad at (explaining things). The podcast took off (100m+ streams), my twitter blew up (450k followers), and my newsletter grew fast (sold in 1 year for millions of dollars).

quote: Proximity is power. Go where your nerds are.
full_excerpt: The funny thing about self improvement is this: sometimes the easiest thing to do is change your surroundings. If you want flowers to bloom, plant your seeds in great soil. Where do you move? Go where your nerds are. Whatever the thing you're nerdy about — where is the highest density of like-minded nerds?

quote: Paul Graham once wrote that every city whispers something in your ear. SF whispers: 'you're not ambitious enough.'
full_excerpt: Paul Graham once wrote that 'every city whispers something in your ear'. LA whispers 'you're not beautiful enough'. NYC whispers 'you're not rich enough'. SF whispers 'you're not ambitious enough'. The whisper isn't always healthy, but it's always motivating. This is why actors move to Hollywood. Why startups move to SF.

quote: You've got a comfortable life. Which is great, if that's what you want. But sounds like it isn't what you want.
full_excerpt: I'm 27 years old, and my life is going 'good'. Good job. Good family. Good apartment. But 'good' isn't great! I really wanna do more. My advice: move. Moving will shake up your routine. Your social circle. Your pace. Your thinking. Your lifestyle.

quote: The people that make it through the decade of suck are the ones who enjoy the game. They don't play to win, they play to play.
full_excerpt: How do you survive the 10 years of flat line progress? The answer is simple: they don't. The people that make it through the 'decade of suck' are the ones who enjoy the game. They don't play to win, they play to play. That's why they keep going, even when they see all their friends getting promotions and buying houses with nice backyards in Connecticut.
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: Don't let your dream float in a magical theoretical bubble. Pop the bubble and find out what you really love.
full_excerpt: Whatever job you THINK you want to do, it's probably wrong. Instead of just talking about it — take it for a 2 week test drive. Try before you buy. I spent 10 years telling everyone I wanted to be a doctor. Those 2 weeks shadowing a surgeon saved me from 8 years of med school and another 20-30 years doing a job that didn't light me up.
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: Give yourself a season of wandering. There is no wrong path when you wander, as long as you're following your curiosity.
full_excerpt: I call this a season of wandering. This is a season where you're going to explore options. You're going to dabble. Try things. I call it 'wandering' because it lets you think creatively. There is no 'wrong path' when you wander, as long as you're following your curiosity and excitement. You're looking for clues, not answers.
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: What feels like play to you, but looks like work to others? That's the moneymaker.
full_excerpt: Start paying attention to what gives you energy, vs. drains you. But the real clue is to figure out: what feels like play to you, but looks like work to others? That's the moneymaker. For me, that's writing. The average person hates writing. They dread the blank page. But I love writing, so I followed that clue. Which led me to starting Milk Road — sold for millions of dollars a year later.
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: You can't ask someone for directions to a place they've never been.
full_excerpt: My parents had very normal 9-to-5 jobs, so I only knew that flavor. They could only teach me what they knew. That's when I learned you can't ask someone for directions to a place they've never been. But instead of complaining about my upbringing, I learned to bring myself up.
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: Luck matters. But if you think it's all luck, you're just a victim of circumstances. Luck matters, but action matters more.
full_excerpt: I am extremely fortunate that I rolled the dice and hit a hard six. So yea, luck matters. But if you think it's all luck, you're just a victim of circumstances. Luck matters, but action matters more.
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: I work on whatever I want, whenever I want, from wherever I want. Energy is the key to success — not hard work.
full_excerpt: Everyone says hard work is the key to success. Bullshit. Energy is the key to success. My energy comes from loving what I do, not from pushing myself to grind harder. I get paid a fortune to do what I would do for free. My short definition of a great career: doing things you love, with people you love.
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: Find the product that's just you pushed out. Get paid a King's ransom for something you'd do for free.
full_excerpt: Forget about hard work. Forget about finding a 'good job'. Find the product that's just you pushed out. You can steal my career goal: 'Get paid a King's ransom for something that I would do for free.' Basically — find a thing that's so you, that doing it is just a natural extension of you being yourself.

quote: Hard work alone doesn't equal success. Hard work sounds fair. But the architect who drew a picture gets paid more than the guy sweating doing construction.
full_excerpt: 'Hard work is the key to success.' Is it? Then shouldn't the guys sweating their ass off doing construction get paid more than the architect who drew a picture of the house? Hard work helps. Certainly. But hard work alone doesn't equal success.

quote: 'Later' and 'Someday' have murdered more dreams than you can count.
full_excerpt: The dangerous lie we tell ourselves is that we can always do that later. [Narrator: he did not do it later. He just stayed doing the same shit he was doing, until the dream faded away.] 'Later' and 'Someday' have murdered more dreams than you can count. F*ck that. Go start the business, tour with the band, backpack thru thailand, whatever it is. Do it. And do it now.

quote: Safety is a serial killer. It operates in a slow, boring fashion. Like a pillow suffocating an old man on a hospital bed.
full_excerpt: Safety murders your ambition. Murders your sense of adventure. Safety is a serial killer. But it operates in a slow, boring fashion. Like a pillow suffocating an old-man on a hospital bed. Your 'safe path' keeps you stuck in an 'OK' relationship, or living in the city you grew up in. Postponing that trip to europe until 'things settle down'.

quote: You're in the Ramen Era. Maximum flexibility, nothing to lose. Warren Buffett would give every dollar he has to trade places with the average 22-year-old.
full_excerpt: If you're 20-27, you're in the Ramen Era. It's a golden period of time where you don't mind sleeping on the couch, you can live off ramen and free refills, you don't have anyone to take care of but yourself. Sure, you're broke and have no skills... but you have maximum flexibility and nothing to lose. Warren Buffett would give every dollar he has, just to trade places with the average 22 year old dipshit who spent the last year doing beer runs for Sigma Chi. That's how powerful youth is.

quote: Things never settle down. You simply stay busy. 'Later' never comes.
full_excerpt: Your 'safe path' keeps you stuck. Postponing that trip to europe until 'things settle down' and you're less busy. But things never settle down. You simply stay busy. And 'later' never comes. Do it. Go on adventures. Go on quests. Find the people you love, and the projects you were put on earth to do.

quote: Everything is an excuse. You get to decide: are you going to find excuses to feel shitty? Or find excuses to feel good?
full_excerpt: Life changes once you realize everything is an excuse. Excuses get a bad rap, but they can be positive or negative. An excuse is simply a reason that you make up and choose to believe in. Woke up tired? Great excuse to skip workout. Or: great excuse to move your body and shake off the sluggish feeling. Same situation. Different excuse. You choose.

quote: Heroes and villains always have the same backstory — pain. The difference is what they choose to do about it.
full_excerpt: Alex Hormozi had a great line: 'Heroes and villains always have the same back story — pain. The difference is what they choose to do about it. Villain says the world hurt me, I'll hurt it back. Hero says the world hurt me, I'm not gonna let it hurt anyone else. Heroes use pain. Villains are used by it.'

quote: Everyone expected him to quit. Either this is an excuse to stop. Or it's an excuse to restart. He went back and restarted. And became someone new.
full_excerpt: Mike Posner walked 2/3rds of the way across America, got bit by a rattlesnake and almost died. Nobody would have faulted him for stopping. But Mike said: 'Everyone expected me to quit. Either this is an excuse to stop. Or it's an excuse to restart. So I went back and restarted. And when I did that, I became someone new.'

quote: There is no such thing as 'life balance.' You don't want balance. You think you do. But you really don't.
full_excerpt: There is no such thing as 'Life Balance.' Not only does life balance not exist — it's not even the right goal. You don't want balance. You think you do. But you really don't. Balance seekers are playing a zero-sum game. You'll end up giving every area of your life 50% effort, so that nothing goes to 0% and nothing gets to 100%. A recipe for mediocrity.
source_title: why the safe path is not actually safe

quote: Instead of choosing Health OR Friends — you go hiking with friends and get both. That's integration. That's how you win.
full_excerpt: The winners of life do integration, not balance. Instead of choosing 'Health OR Friends' → you go hiking with friends (and get both). Instead of choosing 'Work OR Fun' → you pick a career where you genuinely enjoy doing the work. Integration multiplies your time. We all have ~16 waking hours a day, but when you use 1 hour to fill up 3 life buckets — you've multiplied your time.
source_title: why the safe path is not actually safe

quote: Forget job titles. All employees are problem solvers. Are you identifying the A+ problem? Are you solving it?
full_excerpt: Every company has a distribution of talent. Star performers live at the top of the triangle. The whole game is two questions: Are you identifying the A+ problem on a daily, weekly, monthly and annual basis? Are you able to solve that problem — either alone, or by coordinating other people? That's it. That's the whole game.

quote: The ordinary life wasn't for me. I decided that before I knew what the extraordinary life looked like.
full_excerpt: The essay talked about how my life changed when I decided 'the ordinary life isn't for me'. Those first few years were rough. But I knew one thing: I wasn't going to live the same life as everyone around me, even if I didn't know what the alternative was yet.
source_title: how i spent a year strategically broke

quote: 'Who's living the life I want?' — this is a simple, yet powerful question. And you need to be specific.
full_excerpt: The fastest shortcut in self improvement is to find someone who already has what you want and download the blueprint of their habits and mindset. 'Who's living the life I want?' — this is a simple, yet powerful question. And you need to be specific. I wanted to be successful. But then I met a bunch of rich guys who were busy, stressed and divorced and their kids resented them. I didn't want that. So I updated my Blueprint.
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: Turns out there are 10,000x more ways to win than you even realized existed.
full_excerpt: I met a guy who was filthy rich, from selling the conveyor belts that go on treadmills. Then I had an older friend that played ping-pong with me daily. He imports fancy soaps from Italy and resells them to 5-star hotels. He makes $3M a year as the soap guy. The best part? He doesn't even make the soap! He just saw a gap and filled it. Turns out there are 10,000x more 'ways to win' than you even realized existed.
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: If you're 20-27, you're in the Ramen Era. You're broke. But you have maximum flexibility and nothing to lose. That's everything.
full_excerpt: If you're 20-27, you might not realize it yet. But you're in the Ramen Era. It's a golden period of time where you don't mind sleeping on the couch, you can live off ramen and free refills, you don't have anyone to take care of but yourself. Sure, you're broke and have no skills... but you have maximum flexibility and nothing to lose.

quote: The origin of 'Uncle Shaan': I'm just a jackass with wifi. But not knowing has never stopped me from confidently giving an answer.
full_excerpt: Well the simple answer is… I have no clue. I don't know you. I don't know your situation. Remember, I'm just a jackass with wifi. But, 'not knowing' has never stopped me from confidently giving an answer.
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: The 'safe path' is not actually safe. It's dangerous to your dreams.
full_excerpt: My message to you is simple: The 'safe path' is not actually safe. In fact it's dangerous. It's dangerous to your dreams. Safety murders your ambition. Murders your sense of adventure. Safety is a serial killer. But it operates in a slow, boring fashion.

quote: Ben texts ~100 unique people every day. No agenda, just because he likes to do it. We've made millions directly because of it.
full_excerpt: My cofounder Ben Levy finds it very strange why everyone is terrible at keeping in touch. He texts ~100 unique people every day. No agenda, just because he likes to do it. We've directly made millions of dollars just because Ben happened to be staying in touch with someone and they thought of us when an opportunity sprang up. His 'thing' is relationships.

quote: As Tim Ferriss says: most people would rather be unhappy than uncertain. Don't be that person.
full_excerpt: You are probably a 'high achiever' type. And high achievers get really anxious when they don't have an 'answer' for what they're going to do with their life. This causes them to prematurely commit to something — anything. As Tim Ferriss says, most people would rather be unhappy than uncertain. The trick is to name this era and time box it. Call it your Season of Wandering.
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: Even when the scoreboard says 'Life 12, You 0' — they keep playing. Until they get so good that the game has no choice but to give them the win.
full_excerpt: The people that make it through the 'decade of suck' are the ones who enjoy the game. They don't play to win, they play to play. Even when the scoreboard says: 'Life 12, You 0' — they keep playing. They keep playing, until they get so good that the game has no choice but to give them the win.
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: Energy is the key to success. Not hard work. My energy comes from loving what I do, not from pushing myself to grind harder.
full_excerpt: Everyone says hard work is the key to success. Bullshit. Energy is the key to success. My energy comes from loving what I do, not from pushing myself to grind harder. I get paid a fortune to do what I would do for free.
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: As Derek Sivers once said: 'If it's not a Hell Yes, it's a No.'
full_excerpt: If you pop the bubble, you'll know for certain: YES — this is my thing. I'm down to invest a decade becoming great at this. NO — this ain't it. Glad I found out now. MAYBE? — (see 'No'... as Derek Sivers once said, 'if it's not a Hell Yes, it's a No').
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: Instead of choosing Work OR Fun — pick a career where you genuinely enjoy the work. You don't dread Mondays.
full_excerpt: The winners of life do integration, not balance. Instead of choosing 'Work OR Fun' → you pick a career where you genuinely enjoy doing the work (you don't dread Mondays). Instead of choosing 'Career OR Family' → you build a career where you get paid for results, so you can make a ton of money, and have the freedom of time to spend with family.
source_title: why the safe path is not actually safe

quote: The time test: if you came to work for 1 hour and did as much as your co-worker who sat there for 8 hours — would your boss be mad? If yes, you're in the wrong job.
full_excerpt: I had a job for 1 year, but I didn't like it because I was getting paid for my time, not my results. The time test is this: if you came to work for an hour, then closed your laptop and left, having done as much work as your co-worker who sits there for 8 hours — Would your boss be mad at you or your coworker? 99% of jobs, they'd be mad at you, when they should be mad at the unproductive co-worker.
source_title: why the safe path is not actually safe

quote: SF is the only city where startups are normal and jobs are weird. The high-status thing was low-status here. That's a powerful motivator.
full_excerpt: I realized that SF is the only city in the world where startups are normal, and jobs are weird. The high-status thing was low-status here. That's a powerful motivator. Craig worked at Deloitte — a good job. But when he introduced himself, he had to apologize and make excuses for why he was working at Deloitte.

quote: Life is going 'good'. Good job. Good apartment. But 'good' isn't great.
full_excerpt: I got an email from Abram: 'I'm 27 years old, and my life is going… good. I've got a good job. Good family. Good apartment. But good isn't great! I really wanna do more — but I'm not sure what that even means. Yea more money/success is part of it — but also just feels like I'm wasting my potential.' Sound familiar?

quote: If you've already found it — welcome to the Lucky Bastards Club. If you haven't — you just need to give yourself permission to wander.
full_excerpt: If you've already found it (like me) — welcome to the Lucky Bastards Club. If you haven't yet — don't count yourself out. You just need to give yourself permission to wander. Most will say 'I can't afford to'. Don't have the time. The money. The courage. But you only get one ride on this rollercoaster of life. So, maybe the question is: can you afford not to?
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: Either this is an excuse to stop. Or it's an excuse to restart. He went back and restarted.
full_excerpt: Mike Posner got bit by a rattlesnake walking across America. Almost died. Nobody would have faulted him for stopping. But he said: 'Everyone expected me to quit. Either this is an excuse to stop. Or it's an excuse to restart. So I went back and restarted. And when I did that, I became someone new.'

quote: We all want answers. But like any detective, you don't seek the answer directly. Answers come from clues.
full_excerpt: What are you looking for while you wander? Clues, not answers. You see, we all want answers. But like any detective, you don't seek the answer directly. Answers come from clues. Energy clues: what gives you energy vs. drains you? Blueprint clues: who's already living the life you want?
source_title: the 3-step plan to figuring out what you want

quote: The only thing standing between you and the top 0.1% is: are you willing to be more obsessed than everyone else?
full_excerpt: From the MrBeast leaked memo: the common thread among top creators isn't luck or talent — it's obsession. The willingness to study, iterate, and improve faster than anyone else. MrBeast says: 'I'm going to die making YouTube videos.' That level of commitment is what separates the top from everyone else.

quote: You never actually have 'not enough time.' You just have too many things you said yes to that you should have said no to.
full_excerpt: The real problem isn't time. It's that you've said yes to too many things. Every yes to something is a no to something else. The people who seem to have infinite time have just gotten ruthless about what they say no to.
source_title: why the safe path is not actually safe
